questions.q: What does object-level security (OLS) restrict, as opposed to row-level security?
options: Which workspace a semantic model can be published to
Which rows of a table a role sees
Entire tables or columns, hiding them completely from a role
Whether a refresh schedule runs on time
questions.explain: OLS hides whole tables or columns from a role, so it's as if the object doesn't exist in the model for that role's members — a step beyond RLS, which only filters which rows are returned.

questions.q: Where is OLS most commonly configured, since this lesson's screenshots show it being set up?
options: Directly in Power BI Desktop's Manage roles dialog
In an external tool such as Tabular Editor, connected to the semantic model
In the Power BI service's tenant settings
It cannot be configured outside of DAX measures
questions.explain: Power BI Desktop has no built-in OLS editor. OLS is most commonly set using an external tool like Tabular Editor (or, in newer tooling, TMDL view) connected to the model.

questions.q: What does setting a column's Object Level Security value to 'None' for a role do?
options: It filters the column's values but keeps the column visible
It hides the column entirely from that role's members
It applies a sensitivity label to the column
It deletes the column from the semantic model for everyone
questions.explain: None fully hides the object from the specified role. Default and Read both leave the object visible; None is the value that removes it entirely for that role.

questions.q: What happens to a report visual that still references a column a role's OLS setting has hidden?
options: The visual silently shows a blank value
Power BI automatically removes the reference for that role
The visual returns an error for members of that role
Nothing — OLS only affects Tabular Editor, not published reports
questions.explain: Hiding an object with OLS isn't a quiet change — any visual, measure, or relationship still referencing a hidden object returns an error for that role's members, not a blank value.

questions.q: Before rolling out a new OLS restriction on an existing, widely-used semantic model, what does this lesson recommend?
options: Auditing every report built on the model for references to the object, for the affected role, before publishing
Deleting all existing reports built on the model first
Applying the restriction immediately, since OLS changes are always backward-compatible
Converting the model to DirectQuery mode first
questions.explain: Because hiding an object breaks any reference to it for the affected role, rolling out OLS safely means checking every downstream report for that role's references before publishing the change.
